Hi Maya —

Appreciate the forecast — useful detail. High-level answers up front, then technical ops notes below for your procurement packet: 

Summary (short):
- Billing: short transient bursts are charged against usage (per-token/compute) and will not trigger additional reservation fees for minute-scale spikes; for predictable multi-hour spikes we recommend adding a temporary burst slab (reserved for the window) which can be credit-backed and priced at a lower unit rate than on-demand.
- Autoscale & eviction: reserved slabs have strict priority (no eviction for pinned jobs); shoulder/ephemeral pools are preemptible and will evict based on queue weight + tenant priority. We can set eviction thresholds and headroom multipliers in the SLO so NovaHealth retains X% headroom for critical low-latency flows.

Karthik and Ben — looping you in to add the ops/implementation specifics and a short runbook blurb we can hand to procurement. Can you attach a one-page runbook with thresholds, expected latency impact, and the fallback routing policy?

Next steps: I will draft a one-page summary for procurement and a suggested pricing appendix for short-term burst credit vs temporary reserved slab. If procurement wants a formal addendum we can produce an SLA appendix.

Thanks —

Jonas / Maya —

Adding the ops specifics for your packet. Attaching a short runbook stub with thresholds, expected latency delta, and eviction ordering. Key points:

- Burst charging model: minute-scale bursts are billed as usage against the customer's committed pool (per-token and GPU-minutes). For longer windows (>3 hours continuous at >2x committed throughput) we recommend a short-term reserved slab (temporary commit) which we price as a timeboxed addendum (lower per-unit cost, subject to minimum hours).

- Autoscale thresholds (default suggestion):
  * Scale-up trigger: sustained 95th percentile GPU utilization > 78% for 90s across >2 GPUs in pool.
  * Scale-down: sustained 95th percentile < 40% for 5m.
  * Eviction priority: ephemeral preemptible > shoulder reserved > pinned reserved. Preemptible jobs see eviction notice via webhook 30s before eviction.

- Headroom guidance: set a 12% latency headroom for low-latency endpoints (conversational production); set a 25% headroom for batch/fine-tune workloads.

- Fallback routing: on eviction or capacity saturation we route to either (a) lower-cost quantized variant of the model pinned to reserved pool, or (b) regional hosted fallback in a supported region. This is configurable per-route in the route policy.

Attachment: ops_burst_runbook_stub.pdf (one-page runbook)

Let me know if you want tighter thresholds — we can template by endpoint type.

—Karthik
